_README: T282 HAND ADJUDICATION of every citation the checker flagged that the
keyword adjudicator in population-table.py could not decide.
KEYED BY TEXT, NEVER BY LINE NUMBER, and that is not a style choice -- it is
this task's own rule applied to this task's own artefact.
The first version of this file keyed on 'file:LINE:cited'. Merging current
main moved .softhouse/tasks.json:4195 to :4203, the key stopped matching, and
the site silently reverted to UNADJUDICATED. That is exactly P-80 -- 'a
corrected cardinal rots in every place it was restated; THE COUNT IS THE SAME
DEFECT AS THE LINE NUMBER' -- and DEC-2's C-4, 'an ordinal used as an
identifier goes wrong silently; a NAME goes wrong loudly'. An adjudication
table for a citation-rot defect, keyed on an ordinal into a moving file, would
have been the next instance of the thing it documents.
So: each entry names the FILE, the CITED ID, and a stable FRAGMENT of the
gloss ('gloss_contains'). A fragment that matches nothing is reported LOUDLY
by population-table.py rather than silently dropping the verdict -- because a
key that stops matching must look different from a site nobody judged.
Every entry carries its REASON: a verdict with no reason is not a verdict.
Decided by reading the recorded gloss against BOTH rules' text in patterns.md.

verdicts.gloss_contains: not found" is a statement about the search
verdicts.reason: P-70 IS '"not found" is a statement about the search'. Correctly cited. The gloss ran on into a following sentence about the fail-open linter's CORPUS, and that is what scored P-76.

verdicts.gloss_contains: measure both terms, in the live artefact
verdicts.reason: A CONJUNCTION gloss. '**P-67 / P-69** - measure both terms, in the live artefact, at the moment of use' states THREE rules at once: both terms (P-67), moment of use (P-69), live artefact (P-63). Two of the three are cited; the uncited one won the score.
The 'gloss' is a MEASUREMENT REPORT ('was PASS exit 0 at 36 parity vectors and 4,034 cells'), not rule text. The trailing-id extractor over-reached into a results line.
The same measurement-report line as SWEEP.txt, quoted into the handoff. Same adjudication.

verdicts.gloss_contains: prediction commit is a parent of the evidence commit
verdicts.reason: The gloss is a procedural aside about commit ancestry, and restates neither P-9 nor P-17.

verdicts.gloss_contains: conclusion, wrong reason, propagated into a durable file
verdicts.reason: ADJACENT PAIR, not adjudicable from the text alone. P-11 = 'the code can be RIGHT and its stated reason WRONG'. P-12 = 'a right conclusion on a wrong reason RECURS IN THE ARTEFACT written to record it'. The gloss 'conclusion, wrong reason, PROPAGATED INTO A DURABLE FILE' leans P-12, but P-11 is P-12's own premise. Left for the author rather than guessed.

RELATED PAIR. P-58 = 'when N attempts disagree about a tool, COUNT THE PROGRAMS before you count the votes'. P-75 = 'grep and rg in an agent shell are not the programs you think'. The gloss states the host FACT (P-75) inside an argument for the METHOD (P-58). Both defensible.

verdicts.gloss_contains: the fork point, MEASURED, not assumed
verdicts.reason: P-71 IS 'a worker's fork point is UNPREDICTABLE: MEASURE IT, NEVER ASSERT IT', and the gloss is 'the fork point, MEASURED, not assumed'. Exactly right. P-24 ('an assertion about what happens ON MERGE can only be tested BY MERGING') won on a shared token alone.
The 'gloss' is a MARKDOWN HEADING about a guard handling exit codes correctly, which is P-81's own subject. Correctly cited; P-93 won on the token 'guard'.

verdicts.gloss_contains: The exact edit is recorded in T154's handoff
verdicts.reason: The gloss ends 'apply it, and DRIVE IT RED first', which is P-22's remedy ('a guard, a canary, or a control that cannot fail is worse than none'). Correctly cited; the extractor swallowed a file path.

verdicts.gloss_contains: Sweep the concept, not the sentence
verdicts.reason: Inside one long JSON string the extractor bound the span belonging to the NEIGHBOURING '(P-26)' citation. The text is not P-40's gloss at all.
The gloss is 'quote by EXTRACTION', which is P-46's remedy ('a fabricated capture excerpt survived into merged evidence'). Correctly cited.

verdicts.gloss_contains: did not merely fail to run, it RAN
verdicts.reason: NOT the P-86 off-by-one -- an INDEPENDENT drift, and the strongest signal in the entire population (score 21). Gloss: 'the guard did not merely fail to run, it RAN, wrote its answer down, and the summary line above it said the opposite'. That is P-79 almost verbatim ('EVIDENCE NOT MISSING, UNREAD. A recorded predicate that no summary consults'). The cited P-69 is 'the measured claim went stale between the review and the revision', a different rule entirely.

The gloss is 'three consecutive passes have shipped STALE line numbers', which is P-69 ('the measured claim went STALE between the review and the revision'). Correctly cited. RETAINED THOUGH IT NOW MATCHES NOTHING, and the reason is worth knowing: the text is still in tasks.json, but the site is no longer FLAGGED. Adding P-96 to patterns.md changed the rare-token frequencies the scorer derives FROM THE REGISTER, and this borderline site fell below the reporting margin. THE REGISTER IS THE YARDSTICK, so growing it moves borderline verdicts -- here in the correct direction, since the citation was right all along. population-table.py reports this entry as a STALE KEY on every run rather than dropping it silently.

verdicts.gloss_contains: make the second site READ the first, do not restate the cardinal
verdicts.reason: Gloss 'make the second site READ the first, do not restate the cardinal' is P-80. This IS the P-86 off-by-one; the keyword adjudicator missed it only because the phrasing differs from the other seven instances.

verdicts.gloss_contains: cite the rule TEXT beside any P-number
verdicts.reason: The gloss is 'cite the rule TEXT beside any P-number', which is P-86 itself. Correctly cited; the score leaked into surrounding JSON punctuation. THIS IS THE ENTRY WHOSE LINE-NUMBER KEY ROTTED ON MERGE (4195 -> 4203) and forced this file onto text keys.
